records.claim: Earth's rotational speed is about 1,674.7 km/h (465.2 m/s) at the equator, decreasing to zero at the poles.
records.passage: Earth's rotational speed is about 1,674.7 km/h (1,040.6 mph; 465.2 m/s; 1,526.2 ft/s) at the equator, but it decreases with latitude, becoming zero at the poles.

records.claim: At 45° latitude, the speed is roughly 1,184.2 km/h.
records.passage: At middle latitudes, the speed decreases; for example, at 45° latitude, the speed is roughly 1,184.2 km/h (735.8 mph) (1674.7  ×  cos (45°)).

records.claim: The length of a day has increased by about 2.3 milliseconds per century since the 8th century BCE.
records.passage: Analysis of historical astronomical records shows a slowing trend; the length of a day has increased by about 2.3 milliseconds per century since the 8th century BCE.

records.claim: Near Earth's surface, the acceleration due to gravity is 9.8 m/s2.
records.passage: Near Earth's surface, the acceleration due to gravity, accurate to 2 significant figures, is 9.8 m/s2 (32 ft/s2).

narration.text: Earth stops spinning for one second.
But you keep moving at 465 metres per second.
At the equator, that's about 1,675 kilometres per hour, heading east.
Gravity pulls down at 9.8 metres per second squared.
At 45 degrees latitude, it's still about 1,184 kilometres per hour.
Only near the poles would the stop feel gentle.
